description_full: ServiceNow, Inc. provides cloud-based solution for digital workflows in the North America, Brazil, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Asia Pacific, and internationally. The company provides asset management, integrated risk management, IT service management, Operational Technology management, Security Operations, strategic portfolio management, IT operations management products; customer service management product; field service management applications; and sales and order management services. It also offers human resources delivery; legal and contract operations; workplace service delivery products; app engine product; automation engine; platform privacy and security product; and source-to-pay operations. In addition, the company provides RaptorDB, a database built to manage workloads at scale; ServiceNow Impact that provides customers with software tools, guided plans, and AI-driven recommendations; customer support; and workflow data fabric. It serves government, financial services, healthcare and life science, manufacturing, Public Sector, retail, technology, and Telecom sectors through service providers and resale partners. The company has a strategic collaboration with Cohesity, Inc. to develop, operate, and safeguard autonomous AI agents and data with enterprise-grade reliability; and with ServiceNow to Advance Ai-Powered Solution for Mission-Critical Infrastructure Monitoring. The company was formerly known as Service-now.com and changed its name to ServiceNow, Inc. in May 2012. ServiceNow, Inc. has a strategic alliance with Accenture for integrated risk management and third-party risk management solutions, and with Tech Mahindra to validate and deliver production-ready, industry-specific enterprise AI and automation solutions at scale. ServiceNow, Inc. was founded in 2004 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

financial_summary: ServiceNow, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $106.1B market cap on $13.3B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +22% over the past three years and +29% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 44% against a 11% cost of capital — a 32-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 77% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $4.6B in free cash flow — roughly 34 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.11× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 83× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.7%, a thin return of capital, and stock-based comp at 15% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

prof: ROIC of 44% clears the cost of capital of 11.2% by 32pp, the mark of a value creator.

Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.44 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 2.1x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 22%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.2x, 6.5% of sales), a maintenance pace.
